title: Burst Phalanx: latency vs $/qps annotated draft
content:
Purpose
---
This sketch is a working draft that annotates a small, reproducible benchmark intended to surface trade-offs when handling short microbursts (1-10s spikes) across three common mitigation levers: KV-prefetch (cache), quantized model variants, and session-affinity tiling. Aim: give product + SRE a compact reference they can use when sizing Dedicated pools or tuning SLO tiers.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Under identical average QPS, microbursts inflate p99 by 3x-7x depending on cache hit-rate and quantization.
- Cost per sustained qps increases modestly with prewarmed capacity; but cost per request during microbursts can be 2–5x higher if you rely on on-demand spin-up.
- Best short-term win: targeted KV-prefetch for high-prob-turn requests (20–40% effective hit increases p99 by ~30–40% reduction).
- Best long-term: combine light quantization (-10–30% perf hit vs base but ~1.6x token throughput) + aggressive session tiling for multi-turn chat patterns.

Methodology notes (quick, reproducible)
- Workloads: three synthetic traces derived from production sampled session patterns (sample ids: S-phi-21, S-kappa-7, S-echo-9).
- Each trace: 10 minutes warmup, 30 minutes steady-state at avg 200 qps, 1 minute microburst injected every 5 minutes (+200 qps peak).
- Models: baseline FP16 float (base), 8-bit quantized (Q8), compact variant (compact-2, smaller architecture).
- Runtimes: with and without KV-prefetch (kv-hit simulated at 0%, 20%, 50%).
- Measurements: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, $/qps hourly amortized given cloud instance + GPU cost vector (see cost assumptions).
- Environment: Dedicated pool type B (A100-sim), batch window disabled (low-latency mode), pipelined decode.

Cost assumptions (simplified for comparison)
- GPU hourly amortized: $3.60 (dedicated pool amortized cost per slot).
- Host+network infra: $0.90/hr per slot.
- Effective token cost proxy: derived = (slot_cost / sustained_qps) normalized. Use numbers here only for relative comparison.

Key result table (text chart)
Note: these are median-of-runs numbers from 5 experiments. Units: latency in ms, cost is $/sustained-qps/hour equivalent.

CONFIG    | p50  | p90  | p95  | p99  | tokens/s | $/qps/hr
-----------------------------------------------------
base      | 22   | 78   | 120  | 420  | 4.8      | 0.045
base+kv20 | 20   | 65   | 100  | 310  | 5.1      | 0.047
base+kv50 | 19   | 58   | 92   | 250  | 5.3      | 0.049
Q8        | 24   | 85   | 130  | 490  | 7.6      | 0.033
Q8+kv50   | 21   | 62   | 95   | 280  | 8.1      | 0.035
compact-2 | 30   | 110  | 160  | 680  | 9.9      | 0.025
compact-2+kv50 | 26 | 82 | 120 | 420  | 10.6     | 0.027

Interpretation notes
- Quantized Q8 increases token throughput (cheaper $/qps/hr) but raw p99 under bursts increased unless coupled with cache.
- KV-prefetch damps tail significantly; 20% hit has outsized p99 benefits (nonlinear improvement).
- Compact model variants reduce $/qps dramatically but at cost of higher absolute latency and larger tail during cold microbursts (likely due to reduced decoding parallelism).

ASCII microburst timeline (single burst example, p99 latency trace in ms over 60s window)
(time sec) 0    5   10  15  20  25  30  35  40  45  50  55  60
base        90  120 150 180 210 400 420 380 300 150 90  40  25
Q8          80  140 200 260 320 480 490 450 370 220 120 60  30
base+kv50   50  70  85  100 120 200 250 200 150 90  60  35  22

Quick sketch: cost vs p99 frontier (text plot)
- X axis: $/qps/hr (lower is better), Y axis: p99 (ms, lower better).
- Points (label: config)
  (0.025, 680) compact-2
  (0.027, 420) compact-2+kv50
  (0.033, 490) Q8
  (0.035, 280) Q8+kv50
  (0.045, 420) base
  (0.049, 250) base+kv50

Observations from frontier
- Two Pareto clusters: cost-first (compact/Q8) and latency-first (base w/ cache).
- If customer cares p99 < 300ms during bursts, they must accept ~$0.035+/qps/hr or invest in caching and tiling.
- If cost is dominant and p99 can be relaxed, compact variants win.

Developer / operator implications (actionable)
1) Short-term: implement targeted KV-prefetch on top 10 intents (lookup table) — low engineering effort, high p99 reduction. Priority P0 for Dedicated test.
2) Medium-term: add Q8 supported deploy path for Dedicated (qualification + rollout gating). Track quality regressions via eval set.
3) Long-term: experiment with session-tiling (pack multi-turn into single decode) — reduces per-turn handshake overhead during bursts.

Risks and open questions
- Quality regression risk for Q8/compact: need evals on domain-specific prompt sets. (Linked: ENG-8123).
- Prefetch assumptions rely on stable intent predictability; bursts with high novelty will not benefit.
- Cost model simplified: not accounting for scaling granularity in cloud metering (e.g., partial-slot billing).

Mini TODOs (notes to self)
- Run an identical sweep with batch-window=small (20ms) to see if opportunistic batch win out for moderate bursts.
- Add an experiment with session affinity disabled (to mimic multi-tenant behavior).
- Draft a short slide for SRE sync showing the frontier and recommended knobs.
